page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-24-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes a 504 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. Memory capacity is 186.0 GB, providing 7.75 GB of RAM per core. The server is equipped with 1343 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 4 devices, and it does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in single-core operations, including a Geekbench single-core score of 2321.0, single-threaded gzip compression at 36.68 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 15.42 GB/sec, and Geekbench text processing at 2781.0. It also demonstrates top-tier performance in LLM text generation for small models at 394.37 tokens/sec. Strong performance is observed in Geekbench multi-core, Geekbench image processing, static web serving throughput, and small-model LLM prompt processing. Average performance is recorded for multi-core stress-ng, memory bandwidth, and medium model LLM inference.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high density of memory and local NVMe storage relative to its 24 vCPUs, making it a resource-dense option for workloads requiring fast local disk access and substantial RAM without the overhead of higher vCPU tiers. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks and database operations perform in the average tier, indicating potential bottlenecks for memory-bound or highly concurrent database workloads that exceed cache limits.

This server configuration is suitable for memory-intensive applications, local database hosting, text processing pipelines, single-threaded compression tasks, and small-scale LLM inference. The combination of 186 GB RAM and 1343 GB of local NVMe SSD storage supports workloads such as caching layers, web serving, and software compilation.
